title: Add audit log events for Dedicated burst config changes
author: Benji Okafor
body:
Context
Dedicated burst capacity introduces tenant-scoped configuration (enablement, caps, tiers, and temporary overrides). For enterprise + regulated customers, Security/Compliance requires auditable evidence of who changed what, when, and from where (Console vs API vs internal tooling), including support/admin overrides.

This PR adds first-class audit log events for burst configuration mutations and ties them to RBAC permissions, so both external customer admins and Redwood operators generate consistent audit records.

What’s included
- New audit events emitted on tenant burst config writes:
  - dedicated.burst.enable_updated (enable/disable)
  - dedicated.burst.limits_updated (max burst ratio / absolute cap / cooldown window)
  - dedicated.burst.priority_tier_updated (gold/silver/standard)
  - dedicated.burst.override_applied (temporary override with TTL)
  - dedicated.burst.override_revoked (manual revoke)
  - dedicated.burst.override_expired (system expiry)
- Audit payload includes:
  - tenant_id, actor (user/service), actor_type, request_id
  - source (console|public_api|internal_tooling|system)
  - before/after diff (redacted where applicable)
  - reason / change_ticket (optional; required for internal overrides)
  - override_ttl_seconds (when relevant)
- RBAC enforcement updates:
  - Separate permission gate for override actions vs normal config edits
  - Internal support role can apply override only with change_ticket + TTL
- Backfill-compatible behavior:
  - Emits events only for new writes; no retroactive historical backfill in this PR
  - Safe no-op if audit sink is unavailable (still blocks write only if policy requires)

Non-goals
- Not adding UI work in Console (that’s handled in the Console PR reading these events)
- Not changing retention policy or customer export pipeline

Implementation details
- Control plane write path now calls audit.AuditLogger with structured event names and a typed payload. The payload uses a stable schema to minimize downstream breakage.
- “Before” values come from the persisted tenant config read prior to apply; “after” values come from the validated, normalized config.
- Added a small helper to compute JSON patch-like diffs, with explicit allowlist of fields to log (prevents accidentally logging future sensitive fields).
- Override expiration event is emitted by the existing TTL reconciler when it clears override state.

Files / areas changed (high level)
- services/control-plane/tenants/burst_config_mutation.go
- services/control-plane/tenants/rbac/permissions.yaml
- services/audit/events/dedicated_burst_events.go
- services/audit/schema/event_catalog.json
- services/control-plane/reconcilers/burst_override_ttl_reconciler.go
- proto/controlplane/v1/tenants.proto (audit source enum + change_ticket field)
- tests/control-plane/burst_config_audit_test.go
- tests/audit/event_schema_validation_test.go

Example audit payload (illustrative)
Event: dedicated.burst.limits_updated
Fields: tenant_id=tnt_8f3… actor_type=user actor_id=usr_19a… source=console request_id=req_7c0… change_ticket="" before.max_burst_ratio=1.0 after.max_burst_ratio=1.5 before.cooldown_seconds=900 after.cooldown_seconds=900

Operational notes
- If audit sink latency spikes, we batch-and-fire with bounded queue; if queue fills, we drop audit events and increment audit_dropped_total with labels (event_name, source). Internal override writes can optionally be configured to fail-closed via policy (not enabled by default).

Testing
- Unit tests: verifies event names, payload allowlist, diff correctness, and redaction behavior
- Integration-ish tests: tenant config update emits exactly one event; override expiration emits system event
- Schema validation test ensures event_catalog.json includes the new events and required fields

Rollout
- Behind existing burst feature flag; only tenants with burst enabled will exercise most mutations
- No migration required; event catalog is additive

Notes for reviewers
- Security: please confirm the allowlist matches expectations and that override actions are permissioned correctly
- Control plane: please verify we’re not increasing write latency materially (audit emission is async by default)

Follow-ups
- Wire audit events into customer-visible export/report (tracked separately)
- Add documentation snippet to burst audit logging page (docs repo PR)

Refs
- Linear: ENG-4816 (burst config API), ENG-4870 (security review: audit events)
- Related PRs: pr-23741 (tenant burst config schema), pr-23758 (admission controller skeleton)
commits: control-plane: emit audit events on burst config mutations
audit: add dedicated burst event definitions + schema catalog entries
rbac: gate burst overrides behind dedicated permission
reconciler: emit override_expired event when TTL clears override
tests: add burst config audit coverage + schema validation
review_conversation: Marcus Lin: Can we ensure we never log raw request bodies / unknown future fields? The diff helper should be allowlist-based, not denylist. Also, overrides need a distinct permission so support can’t silently change customer economics.

Benji Okafor: Updated diff helper to strict allowlist (explicit burst fields only). Added dedicated.burst.override permission and updated internal_support role. Also added a test that fails if a new burst field isn’t explicitly allowlisted.
Naomi Feldman: For regulated customers, we need a “change ticket” or justification string on internal overrides, plus a stable source field that differentiates system expiry vs human revoke.

Benji Okafor: Added change_ticket to override apply/revoke API paths (required when actor_type=service and source=internal_tooling). Added dedicated.burst.override_expired event emitted by TTL reconciler with source=system.
Ethan Park: The audit emitter is async—what happens if the queue fills? Also please confirm we won’t block tenant writes if audit is down.

Benji Okafor: Queue is bounded; on overflow we drop and increment audit_dropped_total. Writes do not block by default. Added config knob audit.fail_closed_for_override_actions (default false) for future policy tightening.
Jordan Lee: Please keep event names consistent with other Dedicated audit events and ensure deterministic payload ordering for downstream hashing.

Benji Okafor: Renamed events to dedicated.burst.* namespace to match catalog. Payload is structured; JSON serialization uses stable field ordering via the typed struct marshaler. Added a small golden test to prevent accidental renames.
requested_changes: Add strict allowlist diffing + separate RBAC permission for overrides
Require change_ticket for internal override actions
Emit system event for TTL-based override expiry
release_notes: Dedicated: Added audit log events for burst enable/disable, limit changes, priority tier updates, and admin override lifecycle (applied/revoked/expired). Override actions are now gated by a separate RBAC permission.
